biography.plain_text: Sea Shepherd Conservation Society is a United States nonprofit dedicated to protecting marine wildlife and ocean habitats. Its work combines investigation, documentation and direct intervention against destructive activity at sea. Part of a conservation movement dating to 1977, the society operates its own campaigns separately from Sea Shepherd Global and other national organisations.

long_biography.plain_text:
In the Gulf of California, Sea Shepherd Conservation Society works with the Mexican Navy to protect the critically endangered vaquita porpoise. Its crews remove illegal gillnets and abandoned fishing gear, while drone surveillance extends their monitoring range. Retrieved nets are taken to the naval base at San Felipe for shredding and preparation for recycling.

Contributions pay for the society's conservation campaigns, and volunteers contribute their time to work at sea and on land. Public tax filings disclose programme spending, grants and directors, alongside the organisation's annual income and operating expenses.
